newsitem.title: USA: Two-term councilman elected San Antonio mayor.
newsitem.headline: Two-term councilman elected San Antonio mayor.

text.p: Two-term city councilman Howard Peak defeated longtime community activist Kay Turner in a heated mayoral runoff in San Antonio on Tuesday, city election officials said.
Peak, 48, who ran on a platform of fiscal conservatism but was labelled "mister tax and spend" by his opponent, won with 57 percent of the vote to Turner's 43 percent.
"It was a group effort, and it will be a group effort to lead the city of San Antonio," Peak said at his campaign headquarters after Turner conceded.
Turner, 50, was the top vote getter in a seven-way primary on May 3 that ousted incumbent Mayor Bill Thornton.

But she was outspent in the campaign and blamed "mudslinging" by Peak for contributing to her defeat in her third bid for mayor. One advertisement broadcast by Peak labelled Turner "the great pretender" and focused on her involvement in a business that later filed for bankruptcy.
During the campaign, Peak did not specify how he planned to deal with a possible multi-million budget shortfall expected to be unveiled by city officials in June.
A one-time city planner, Peak also avoided committing himself to a smoking ban being considered by the city council in this tourist town in central Texas.
